contents.html: Risk-based approaches to determine assurance levels required to protect online transactions, and the associated technical and procedural controls, have been adopted at the federal level and similar standards ratified within international standards organizations. However, international government identity programs are developing their own standards and guidelines rather than adopting a smaller set of existing standards. In the private sector, industry has developed profiles to meet the needs of their business model and partners, as well as their risk tolerance, but there is not agreement among organizations as to which identity assurance standard is the most holistic and therefore capable of being adopted cross-industry.
contents.html_ja: オンライン取引を保護するために必要な保証レベルと、関連する技術的および手続き的な管理策を決定するためのリスクベースの手法は、連邦レベルで採用されており、同様の標準が国際標準化機関内で承認されています。しかし、各国政府のアイデンティティプログラムは、より少数の既存標準を採用するのではなく、独自の標準とガイドラインを策定しています。民間部門では、産業界が、自らのビジネスモデルとパートナー、およびそのリスク許容度のニーズを満たすプロファイルを策定してきましたが、どのアイデンティティ保証の標準が最も包括的であり、したがって業界横断的に採用できるかについては、組織間で合意がありません。

contents.html: Information security management system (ISMS) standards provide a set of processes and corresponding security controls to establish a governance, risk, and compliance structure for information security for an organization, an organizational unit, or a set of processes controlled by a single organizational entity. An ISMS requires a risk-based approach to security that involves selecting specific security controls based on the desired risk posture of the organization and requires measuring effectiveness of security processes and controls. An ISMS requires a cycle of continual improvement for an organization to continue assessing security risks, assessing controls, and improving security to remain within risk tolerance levels by balancing security and risk tolerances.
contents.html_ja: 情報セキュリティマネジメントシステム（ISMS）の標準は、組織、組織単位、または単一の組織エンティティが管理する一連のプロセスについて、情報セキュリティのガバナンス、リスク、コンプライアンスの構造を確立するためのプロセス一式と、それに対応するセキュリティ管理策を提供します。ISMS には、セキュリティに対するリスクベースの手法が必要であり、組織が望ましいとするリスク態勢に基づいて特定のセキュリティ管理策を選択するとともに、セキュリティプロセスと管理策の有効性を測定する必要があります。ISMS には、セキュリティとリスク許容度の均衡を取りながら、組織がリスク許容度の範囲内にとどまるよう、セキュリティリスクと管理策を継続的に評価し、セキュリティを改善していくサイクルが必要です。

contents.html: In addition, certain process evaluation programs should be considered. One program for mitigating the risk of maliciously tainted and counterfeit parts in IT products, to help assure security and integrity in these products, is ISO/IEC 20243-2:2018 Information technology -- Open Trusted Technology Provider<sup>TM</sup> Standard (O-TTPS) -- Mitigating maliciously tainted and counterfeit products -- Part 2: Assessment procedures for the O-TTPS and ISO/IEC 20243-1:2018. As noted under the ISMS core area above, this standard identifies secure engineering best practices, including secure management of the IT products, components, and their supply chains. While it does not cover product evaluations, it does provide for process evaluation. Such evaluations determine if a technology provider, component supplier, or distributor meets all the process requirements in the standard throughout a product’s life-cycle (design through disposal). This would include the product development and secure engineering methods they use and the supply chain security they provide.
contents.html_ja: 加えて、特定のプロセス評価プログラムを検討すべきです。IT 製品における悪意をもって汚染された部品や偽造部品のリスクを軽減し、これらの製品のセキュリティと完全性の保証に役立てるプログラムの 1 つが、ISO/IEC 20243-2:2018 Information technology -- Open Trusted Technology Provider<sup>TM</sup> Standard (O-TTPS) -- Mitigating maliciously tainted and counterfeit products -- Part 2: Assessment procedures for the O-TTPS and ISO/IEC 20243-1:2018 です。上記の ISMS のコア領域で述べたように、この標準は、IT 製品、コンポーネント、およびそれらのサプライチェーンの安全な管理を含む、セキュアエンジニアリングのベストプラクティスを特定しています。製品評価は対象としていませんが、プロセス評価を規定しています。この評価では、技術の提供者、コンポーネントの供給者、または販売者が、製品のライフサイクル全体（設計から廃棄まで）を通じて、この標準のすべてのプロセス要件を満たしているかどうかを判定します。これには、彼らが用いる製品開発とセキュアエンジニアリングの方法、および提供するサプライチェーンセキュリティが含まれます。

contents.html: 7.7 Network Security

contents.html: Network security standards provide security requirements and guidelines on processes and methods for the secure management, operation and use of information, information networks, and their inter-connections. Such standards-based technologies can help to assure the confidentiality and integrity of data in motion, assure electronic commerce, and provide for a robust, secure and stable network and Internet.
contents.html_ja: ネットワークセキュリティの標準は、情報、情報ネットワーク、およびそれらの相互接続の安全な管理、運用、利用のためのプロセスと方法について、セキュリティ要件とガイドラインを提供します。こうした標準に基づく技術は、転送中のデータの機密性と完全性を保証し、電子商取引を保証するとともに、堅牢で安全かつ安定したネットワークとインターネットの実現に役立ちます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p53と照合。見出し・段落・箇条の項目を分ける

contents.html_ja: IoT ネットワークは、多数のプロトコルと物理リンクを用いて展開されます。適切なメッセージングおよび通信プロトコルの選択は、ユースケースと、各システムのセキュリティ要件によって決まります。
contents.html: IoT networks are deployed using a multitude of protocols and physical links. Selecting the appropriate messaging and communication protocols depends on the use case and security requirements for each system.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p53と照合。見出し・段落・箇条の項目を分ける

contents.html: One characteristic of IoT is the potential for spontaneous connections (due to the networking) without a system view. Viewed in this way the IoT could not be ‘planned’ nor secured well using traditional approaches to security since system compositional or emergent properties would never be seen by a risk manager. The network interfaces in these loosely coupled systems represent attack surfaces. Therefore, without a system asset definition and subsequent threat analysis the security design is very unlikely to be useful.
contents.html_ja: IoT の特徴の 1 つは、（ネットワーク化によって）システムとしての視点なしに、自発的な接続が生じる可能性があることです。このように見ると、システムの構成的特性や創発的特性がリスク管理者の目に入ることがないため、IoT を従来のセキュリティの手法で「計画」したり、適切に保護したりすることはできません。これらの疎結合なシステムにおけるネットワークインターフェースは、攻撃対象領域となります。したがって、システム資産の定義とその後の脅威分析がなければ、セキュリティ設計が役に立つ可能性はきわめて低くなります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p53と照合。段落

contents.html: Radio Frequency (RF) connections may be based on industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) radio band, cellular data, or other standards. RF interference should be considered as a source of risk for IoT deployments. Individual sensors may be disabled or degraded by RF interference. This could be inadvertent, e.g., use of a poorly shielded microwave oven near an IP based security camera; or malicious, e.g., use of a cell-phone jammer to prevent long-term evolution (LTE)-connected motion sensors from transmitting activity to a security officer monitoring station
contents.html_ja: 無線周波数（RF）接続は、産業・科学・医療用（ISM）無線帯域、セルラーデータ、またはその他の標準に基づく場合があります。RF 干渉は、IoT 展開におけるリスクの発生源として考慮すべきです。個々のセンサーは、RF 干渉によって無効化されたり、性能が低下したりする場合があります。これは、たとえば、IP ベースの防犯カメラの近くでシールドの不十分な電子レンジを使用するなどの不注意によるものの場合もあれば、たとえば、携帯電話ジャマーを使用して、Long Term Evolution（LTE）接続の動体センサーが警備員の監視所に活動を送信するのを妨げるなどの悪意によるものの場合もあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p54と照合。段落

These protocols extend over the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layers, i.e., physical, link, network, transport, and application layers.

contents.html: A variety of organizations are involved in developing network security standards. The IETF developed RFC 2196 provides a general and broad overview of information security including network security, incident response, or security policies. IETF Security Area Working Groups include: IP Security Maintenance and Extensions, Kitten (GSS-API Next Generation), Managed Incident Lightweight Exchange, Network Endpoint Assessment, Open Authentication, and Transport Layer Security.

contents.html: The IEEE standard, 802.11i-2004, implemented as Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> Protected Access II (WPA2). This amendment to IEEE 802.11 defined Temporal Key Integrity Protocol (TKIP) and Counter Mode Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol (CCMP), which provided more robust data protection mechanisms than Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) affords. The current version of IEEE 802.11 is IEEE 802.11™-2016: IEEE Standard for Information technology – Telecommunications and information exchange between systems Local and metropolitan area networks – Specific requirements – Part 11: Wireless LAN Medium Access Control (MAC) and Physical Layer (PHY) Specifications.
contents.html_ja: IEEE 標準 802.11i-2004 は、Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> Protected Access II（WPA2）として実装されたものです。この IEEE 802.11 の修正は、Temporal Key Integrity Protocol（TKIP）と Counter Mode Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code Protocol（CCMP）を定義し、Wired Equivalent Privacy（WEP）が提供するものよりも堅牢なデータ保護メカニズムを提供しました。IEEE 802.11 の現行バージョンは、IEEE 802.11™-2016: IEEE Standard for Information technology – Telecommunications and information exchange between systems Local and metropolitan area networks – Specific requirements – Part 11: Wireless LAN Medium Access Control (MAC) and Physical Layer (PHY) Specifications です。

contents.html: Physical security standards provide requirements and guidance to prevent unauthorized personnel, attackers or accidental intruders from physically accessing an area, building, room, computer, etc. Such standards can help to ensure that IoT components are not disabled or replaced it with a component that serves the same purpose but is compromised. IoT components may be distributed over a wide area, a remote location or an unattended location where physical access is difficult to restrict.
contents.html_ja: 物理セキュリティの標準は、権限のない要員、攻撃者、または偶発的な侵入者が、区域、建物、部屋、コンピューターなどに物理的にアクセスするのを防ぐための要件とガイダンスを提供します。こうした標準は、IoT コンポーネントが無効化されたり、同じ目的を果たすものの危殆化されたコンポーネントに置き換えられたりしないようにするのに役立ちます。IoT コンポーネントは、広い地域、遠隔地、または物理的なアクセスの制限が困難な無人の場所に分散して配置される場合があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p54と照合。段落

contents.html: There are broadly applicable physical security standards, such as ANSI/ASIS PAP.1-2012 Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection. This standard provides a management approach for the protection of assets by the application of security measures for physical asset protection that can be applied to IoT components and systems.
contents.html_ja: ANSI/ASIS PAP.1-2012 Security Management Standard: Physical Asset Protection など、広く適用できる物理セキュリティの標準があります。この標準は、IoT コンポーネントとシステムに適用できる、物理的資産保護のためのセキュリティ対策の適用による、資産の保護に対するマネジメントの手法を提供します。

contents.html: 7.9 Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring (SACM)
contents.html_ja: 7.9 セキュリティの自動化と継続的監視（SACM）
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p55と照合。見出し

contents.html: Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring (SACM) standards describe protocols and data formats that enable the ongoing, automated collection, monitoring, verification, and maintenance of software, system, and network security configurations, and provide greater awareness of vulnerabilities and threats to support organizational risk management decisions. Automation protocols also include standards for machine-readable vulnerability identification and metrics, platform and asset identification, actionable threat information and policy triggers for actions to respond to threats and policy violations. Automated activities would include a security operation center (SOC) to ensure autonomous and continuing monitoring and evolution of the security state of assets based upon prescribed events.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティの自動化と継続的監視（SACM）の標準は、ソフトウェア、システム、ネットワークのセキュリティ構成の継続的で自動化された収集、監視、検証、維持を可能にし、組織のリスクマネジメントの意思決定を支援するため、脆弱性と脅威についてのより高い認識を提供する、プロトコルとデータ形式を記述します。自動化プロトコルには、機械可読な脆弱性の識別とメトリクス、プラットフォームと資産の識別、実行可能な脅威情報、脅威やポリシー違反に対応する行動のためのポリシートリガーの標準も含まれます。自動化される活動には、所定のイベントに基づいて資産のセキュリティ状態を自律的かつ継続的に監視し進化させることを確保するための、セキュリティオペレーションセンター（SOC）が含まれます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p55と照合。段落

contents.html: While higher-level standards for security automation and continuous monitoring are available and low-level specifications and implementations are in use, they require maturation and shepherding through international standards developing organizations.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティの自動化と継続的監視のより高水準の標準は利用可能であり、低水準の仕様と実装も使用されていますが、これらは成熟させ、国際標準開発組織を通じて導いていく必要があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p55と照合。段落

contents.html: Existing standards include a large body of work under ISO/IEC, IETF, and industry-led efforts (e.g., Cloud Security Alliance, Health Information Trust Alliance [HITRUST], North American Electric Reliability Corporation [NERC] Critical Infrastructure Protection [CIP]) related to asset, configuration, and vulnerability management—the underpinning of a continuous monitoring capability. Other standards include those being developed by the IETF Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring (SACM) Working Group.
contents.html_ja: 既存の標準には、継続的監視能力の基盤である資産、構成、および脆弱性の管理に関連する、ISO/IEC、IETF、および業界主導の取り組み（例: Cloud Security Alliance、Health Information Trust Alliance［HITRUST］、North American Electric Reliability Corporation［NERC］ Critical Infrastructure Protection［CIP］）による多数の成果があります。そのほかの標準には、IETF の Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring（SACM）ワーキンググループが策定中のものがあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p55と照合。段落

contents.html: As with incident management, IT security automation and continuous monitoring is relatively well developed. Security automation and continuous monitoring is much more difficult to implement in ICS. Disruption of finely balanced network communications timing and the lack of in-depth understanding of industrial communications protocols are two major limiting factors that will need to be addressed before this security barrier is more widely used.
contents.html_ja: インシデント管理と同様に、IT のセキュリティ自動化と継続的監視は比較的よく発達しています。ICS では、セキュリティ自動化と継続的監視の実装ははるかに困難です。精緻に均衡の取られたネットワーク通信のタイミングが乱れることと、産業用通信プロトコルに関する深い理解が欠如していることは、このセキュリティ上の障壁がより広く利用される前に対処する必要がある、2 つの大きな制限要因です。

contents.html: Software assurance standards describe requirements and guidance for significantly decreasing the likelihood of software having vulnerabilities, either intentionally designed into the software or accidentally inserted at any time during its life cycle, and that the software functions in the intended manner. This includes custom software, commercial off-the-shelf software, firmware, operating systems, utilities, databases, applications and applets for the Web, software/platform/infrastructure as a service (SaaS, PaaS, IaaS), mobile and consumer devices, etc.

The integrity of the code is also considered an aspect of software assurance. contents.html: Supply chain risk management (SCRM) standards aim to provide the confidence that organizations will produce and deliver information technology products or services that perform as required. They seek to mitigate supply chain-related risks, such as insertion of counterfeits and malicious software, unauthorized production, tampering, theft, and poor quality products and services. IT SCRM standardization requirements include methodologies and processes that enable an organization’s increased visibility into, and understanding of, how technology that they acquire and manage is developed, integrated, and deployed, as well as the processes, procedures, and practices used to assure the integrity, security, resilience, and quality of the products and services. IT SCRM standardization lies at the intersection of cybersecurity and supply chain management and provides a mix of mitigation strategies from both disciplines for a targeted approach to managing IT supply chain risks.
contents.html_ja: サプライチェーンリスクマネジメント（SCRM）の標準は、組織が、要求どおりに機能する情報技術の製品やサービスを製造し、提供するという信頼を提供することを目的としています。これらの標準は、偽造品や悪意あるソフトウェアの挿入、無許可の製造、改ざん、盗難、低品質の製品やサービスなど、サプライチェーンに関連するリスクの軽減を目指します。IT の SCRM 標準化の要件には、組織が調達し管理する技術がどのように開発、統合、展開されているか、また製品とサービスの完全性、セキュリティ、レジリエンス、品質を保証するために用いられるプロセス、手順、実践について、組織の可視性と理解を高める方法論とプロセスが含まれます。IT の SCRM 標準化は、サイバーセキュリティとサプライチェーンマネジメントの接点に位置し、IT サプライチェーンのリスクを管理する的を絞った手法のために、両分野の緩和戦略を組み合わせて提供します。

contents.html: 8.1 Cryptographic Techniques
contents.html_ja: 8.1 暗号技術
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p59と照合。見出し

contents.html: Cryptographic techniques will need adjustments and innovations to accommodate the IoT. Scalability, performance, memory- and power-limited devices, and constrained communication channels all contribute to the cryptographic challenges associated with the IoT. The need for cryptographic algorithms that can work within the confines of a simple electronic device is motivating development of standardized “lightweight cryptography” (LWC). LWC does not imply lightweight security. Rather, the “lightweight” concept refers to design constraints on LWC algorithms evaluated in two separate contexts: software and hardware. In software LWC implementations, smaller code and/or RAM size are preferable. Important measures for hardware LWC implementations are chip size and/or energy consumption.
contents.html_ja: 暗号技術は、IoT に対応するために、調整と革新を必要とします。スケーラビリティ、性能、メモリや電力が限られた機器、制約のある通信チャネルはいずれも、IoT に関連する暗号上の課題の一因となっています。単純な電子機器の制約の範囲内で動作できる暗号アルゴリズムの必要性が、標準化された「軽量暗号」（LWC）の開発の動機となっています。LWC は、軽量なセキュリティを意味するものではありません。「軽量」という概念は、ソフトウェアとハードウェアという 2 つの別個の文脈で評価される LWC アルゴリズムの設計上の制約を指します。ソフトウェアの LWC 実装では、コードサイズおよび／または RAM サイズが小さいことが望まれます。ハードウェアの LWC 実装の重要な尺度は、チップのサイズおよび／またはエネルギー消費です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p59と照合。段落
contents.translation_resolve_note: preferable を「すべきです」と誤って当てた非文法的な訳を直す

contents.html: In some implementations, existing cryptographic standards can support IoT systems. For instance, IoT devices that possess the required resources can use the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) block cipher, a symmetric key encryption algorithm specified in ISO/IEC 18033-3:2010. Additionally, substantial effort has gone into reshaping AES into a solution for lightweight applications. The AES standard has widespread market acceptance.
contents.html_ja: 実装によっては、既存の暗号標準が IoT システムを支えることができます。たとえば、必要な資源を備えた IoT 機器は、ISO/IEC 18033-3:2010 に規定された共通鍵暗号アルゴリズムである Advanced Encryption Standard（AES）ブロック暗号を使用できます。さらに、AES を軽量なアプリケーション向けのソリューションに作り替えるために、多大な努力が払われてきました。AES 標準は、市場で広く受け入れられています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p59と照合。段落

contents.html: Other standards have been developed to specifically support IoT systems. For example, the multipart ISO/IEC 29167 standard provides cryptographic options for the air interface of radio-frequency identification (RFID) components and the multipart ISO/IEC 29192 standard for lightweight cryptography provides cryptographic options for IoT components with constrained processing capabilities. Market acceptance for parts of these standards has not yet occurred.
contents.html_ja: IoT システムを特に支援するために策定された標準もあります。たとえば、複数部構成の ISO/IEC 29167 標準は、無線周波数識別（RFID）コンポーネントの無線インターフェースに暗号の選択肢を提供し、軽量暗号のための複数部構成の ISO/IEC 29192 標準は、処理能力に制約のある IoT コンポーネントに暗号の選択肢を提供します。これらの標準の一部について、市場での受け入れはまだ起きていません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p59と照合。段落

contents.html: Public-key cryptography (PKC), ubiquitous on the Web, may appear as a natural choice since the inconvenience and restrictions of shared secrets are eliminated. However, the computational demands of public-key cryptography, which may not be feasible for tiny IoT devices, must be weighed against the key management and protocol limitations that come with symmetric key cryptography. As an example, and given the immense scale envisioned for IoT applications, certificate revocation, which include resource-hungry activities such as the processing and storage associated with certificate revocation lists (CRLs) or the bandwidth associated with Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP), would have to be compared to the manual process and vulnerability of symmetric key distribution and update.
contents.html_ja: 公開鍵暗号（PKC）は、Web でごく普通に使われており、共有シークレットの不便さと制限がなくなるため、自然な選択に見えるかもしれません。しかし、小さな IoT 機器では実現できない可能性のある公開鍵暗号の計算需要は、共通鍵暗号に伴う鍵管理とプロトコルの制限と比較検討されなければなりません。たとえば、IoT アプリケーションに想定される膨大な規模を踏まえると、証明書失効リスト（CRL）に関連する処理と保存、またはオンライン証明書状態プロトコル（OCSP）に関連する帯域幅といった、資源を大量に消費する活動を伴う証明書失効は、共通鍵の配布と更新の手作業によるプロセスおよびその脆弱性と比較されなければならないでしょう。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p59と照合。段落

contents.html: Existing standards and those being developed address these concerns. Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC), defined in accepted standards such as ISO/IEC 29192-4:2013, is a public-key approach that provides well understood levels of security with smaller keys and signatures than, for example, RSA. ECC has also become entrenched as a "must implement" mechanism in many Internet protocols, such as TLS (RFC 5246), DTLS (RFC 6347), and the Internet Key Exchange for IPsec (RFC 7296). For symmetric key applications (either alone or in conjunction with PKC), light-weight algorithms are defined in ISO/IEC 29192-2. These symmetric ciphers are tuned for limited power devices. Key management guidance is available in publications such as NIST Special Publication 800-57.
contents.html_ja: 既存の標準と策定中の標準は、これらの懸念に対処しています。ISO/IEC 29192-4:2013 などの承認された標準で定義されている楕円曲線暗号（ECC）は、たとえば RSA よりも小さな鍵と署名で、よく理解されたレベルのセキュリティを提供する公開鍵方式です。ECC はまた、TLS（RFC 5246）、DTLS（RFC 6347）、IPsec のためのインターネット鍵交換（RFC 7296）など、多くのインターネットプロトコルで、「実装必須（must implement）」のメカニズムとして定着しています。共通鍵のアプリケーション（単独の場合も、PKC と組み合わせる場合も）向けには、軽量アルゴリズムが ISO/IEC 29192-2 で定義されています。これらの共通鍵暗号は、電力が限られた機器向けに調整されています。鍵管理のガイダンスは、NIST Special Publication 800-57 などの刊行物で入手できます。

contents.html_ja: ブロックチェーンは、IoT セキュリティに革命をもたらす可能性のある、進化中の技術です。ブロックチェーンモデルは、機器間のピアツーピアの相互作用を促し、そのためセキュリティを分散化します。ブロックチェーンはまだ進化の途上にあり、セキュリティメカニズムへの適用可能性もまだよく理解されていないため、ブロックチェーンを通常の相互運用可能な形で使用するための標準は存在しません。しかし、その潜在力は、SDO が注目すべきほど大きなものです。
contents.html: Blockchain is an evolving technology that could revolutionize IoT security. The blockchain model favors peer-to-peer interactions between devices and thus de-centralizes security. Because blockchain is still evolving and its applicability to security mechanisms is still not well understood, no standards exist for using blockchain in a regular interoperable fashion. However, the potential is significant enough that SDOs should be taking note.

contents.html_ja: 8.2 サイバーインシデント管理

contents.html: There are many standards for cyber incident management that cover cyber incident identification, handling, and remediation. Many are applicable to IoT systems. Examples include: HITRUST CSF v9 for reporting information security incidents and weaknesses; IETF RFC 5070 – 2007 for sharing information about computer security incidents; ISO/IEC 29147: 2014 and ISO/IEC 30111: 2013 for vulnerability disclosure and handling process; Organization for the Advancement of Structured Information Standards (OASIS) OpenC2 (draft) for machine to machine exchange of commands to achieve investigative, remediation and/or mitigation effects; and OpenFog Reference Architecture (RA) (February 2017) for tamper response. Some of these standards have widespread market acceptance.
contents.html_ja: サイバーインシデントの特定、対処、是正を扱うサイバーインシデント管理の標準は、数多くあります。その多くは IoT システムに適用できます。例には、情報セキュリティインシデントと弱点を報告するための HITRUST CSF v9、コンピューターセキュリティインシデントについての情報を共有するための IETF RFC 5070 – 2007、脆弱性の開示と対処のプロセスのための ISO/IEC 29147: 2014 と ISO/IEC 30111: 2013、調査、是正および／または緩和の効果を得るためのコマンドの機器間交換のための Organization for the Advancement of Structured Information Standards（OASIS）OpenC2（ドラフト）、改ざん対応のための OpenFog Reference Architecture（RA）（2017年2月）があります。これらの標準の一部は、市場で広く受け入れられています。

contents.html_ja: IoT システムのサイバーインシデント管理について、市場での実装は遅れています。一部の IoT システムは、サイバーセキュリティ上の欠陥を修正するためのソフトウェアパッチを使用できません。そのような場合、サイバーインシデント管理はインシデントの特定には重要ですが、是正には IoT コンポーネントの交換が必要となる場合があります。交換には時間と費用がかかる可能性があります。
contents.html: Market implementations are lagging for cyber incident management for IoT systems. Some IoT systems are not able to use software patches to fix cybersecurity flaws. In such cases, cyber incident management is important for identifying incidents, but remediation may require replacing IoT components. Replacement could be time-consuming and expensive.

contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p61と照合。見出し

contents.html: There are several ISMS standards with market acceptance that are generally applicable to IoT systems or specific IoT applications. The ISA/IEC 62443 series includes security management requirements for Industrial Automation and Control Systems (IACS). ISO 13485:2016 provides management requirements for medical devices and related services. ISO 27799:2016 covers information security management in health using ISO/IEC 27002. ISO/IEC 20243:2015 identifies secure engineering best practices, including secure management of the IT products, components, and their supply chains. ISO/IEC 27001:2013 provides best practices for implementing an ISMS and is being widely used. ISO/IEC 27002:2013 is also being widely used as a reference for selecting security controls when implementing an ISMS.
contents.html_ja: IoT システムまたは特定の IoT アプリケーションに概ね適用でき、市場で受け入れられている ISMS 標準がいくつかあります。ISA/IEC 62443 シリーズには、産業用オートメーションおよび制御システム（IACS）のセキュリティマネジメント要件が含まれています。ISO 13485:2016 は、医療機器と関連サービスのマネジメント要件を規定しています。ISO 27799:2016 は、ISO/IEC 27002 を用いた医療分野の情報セキュリティマネジメントを扱っています。ISO/IEC 20243:2015 は、IT 製品、コンポーネント、およびそれらのサプライチェーンの安全な管理を含む、セキュアエンジニアリングのベストプラクティスを特定しています。ISO/IEC 27001:2013 は、ISMS を実装するためのベストプラクティスを提供しており、広く使われています。ISO/IEC 27002:2013 も、ISMS を実装する際にセキュリティ管理策を選択するための参照として、広く使われています。

contents.html: While there are specific management system standards for some IoT applications, there are other IoT applications that could possibly benefit from a management system standard based upon ISO/IEC 27002. Although ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27002 are widely used, the widespread adoption of these standards to IoT has not yet occurred.

contents.html: A new area of work could be to develop IoT security controls overlay where they would not only specify the security controls, but also could stipulate specific implementation requirements for the controls. For example, NIST SP 800-82 includes a security controls overlay for industrial control systems; and NIST SP 800-161 includes a security controls overlay for supply chain.
contents.html_ja: 新たな作業領域として、セキュリティ管理策を規定するだけでなく、管理策の具体的な実装要件も定めることができる、IoT セキュリティ管理策のオーバーレイの策定が考えられます。たとえば、NIST SP 800-82 には産業用制御システム向けのセキュリティ管理策のオーバーレイが含まれ、NIST SP 800-161 にはサプライチェーン向けのセキュリティ管理策のオーバーレイが含まれています。

contents.html: There are many IT system security evaluation standards with market acceptance that should be relevant to IoT systems. Standards for security requirements for cryptographic modules (e.g., ISO/IEC 19790:2015) and security test requirements for cryptographic modules (e.g., ISO/IEC 24759:2014) are relevant for many types of IoT components. Other examples include: the three-part ISO/IEC 15408 for IT security evaluation; ISO/IEC TR 30104:2015 for guidance on physical security attacks, mitigation techniques and security requirements; and UL 2900 for testable cybersecurity criteria for network-connectable products and systems.
contents.html_ja: IoT システムに関連するはずの、市場で受け入れられている IT システムのセキュリティ評価標準は数多くあります。暗号モジュールのセキュリティ要件の標準（例: ISO/IEC 19790:2015）と、暗号モジュールのセキュリティテスト要件の標準（例: ISO/IEC 24759:2014）は、多くの種類の IoT コンポーネントに関連します。そのほかの例には、IT セキュリティ評価のための 3 部構成の ISO/IEC 15408、物理セキュリティ攻撃、緩和技術、セキュリティ要件に関するガイダンスのための ISO/IEC TR 30104:2015、ネットワーク接続可能な製品とシステムのテスト可能なサイバーセキュリティ基準のための UL 2900 があります。

contents.html: 8.7 Network Security

contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p62と照合。見出し

contents.html: There are many network security standards for various types of networks that are relevant to IoT systems. Examples include: the 3GPP Long-Term Evolution (LTE) for high-speed wireless communication for mobile phones; the Bluetooth wireless standard for exchanging data over short distances from fixed and mobile devices, and building personal area networks; the IETF RFC 7252 for a generic web protocol for the special requirements of the constrained environment of machine-to-machine (M2M) applications; IEC 62591:2016 for industrial wireless sensor networks; the IEEE 1609 family of standards for Wireless Access in Vehicular Environments (WAVE); IEEE 802.11-2016 for Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup>; the OMA Lightweight Machine to Machine Technical Specification, a device management protocol designed for sensor networks and the demands of a machine-to-machine (M2M) environment; and the ZigBee 3.0 specification that enables IoT components from separate IoT systems/applications to communicate.
contents.html_ja: IoT システムに関連する、さまざまな種類のネットワークのためのネットワークセキュリティ標準が数多くあります。例には、携帯電話の高速無線通信のための 3GPP Long-Term Evolution（LTE）、固定機器やモバイル機器から短距離でデータを交換し、パーソナルエリアネットワークを構築するための Bluetooth 無線標準、機器間（M2M）アプリケーションの制約のある環境の特別な要件のための汎用 Web プロトコルである IETF RFC 7252、産業用無線センサーネットワークのための IEC 62591:2016、Wireless Access in Vehicular Environments（WAVE）のための IEEE 1609 ファミリーの標準、Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> のための IEEE 802.11-2016、センサーネットワークと機器間（M2M）環境の要求のために設計された機器管理プロトコルである OMA Lightweight Machine to Machine Technical Specification、別々の IoT システム／アプリケーションの IoT コンポーネント同士が通信できるようにする ZigBee 3.0 仕様があります。

contents.html_ja: セクション 4.3 に挙げた IoT のサイバーセキュリティ上の考慮事項に対処するため、更新や新たな標準が必要となる可能性があります。さらに、これらの既存の標準の多くは、システム全体の視点を欠いたままネットワーク化によって自発的な接続が生じる可能性のある IoT ネットワークに対処するため、更新や新たな標準が必要となる場合があります。そうした IoT システムは、システムの構成的特性や創発的特性をリスク管理者が認識できないため、従来のセキュリティ手法では計画を立てることも適切に保護することもできません。
contents.html: Updates and/or new standards may be needed to deal with the IoT cybersecurity considerations listed in Section 4.3. Additionally, many of these existing standards may require updates and/or new standards to address IoT networks that have the potential for spontaneous connection (due to the networking) without a system view. Such IoT systems cannot be planned or secured well using traditional approaches to security since system compositional or emergent properties would never be seen by a risk manager.

contents.html: IoT components may be in remote and unattended locations where physical access is almost unrestricted. Due to their cost model, very low cost IoT components cannot be protected by physically hardening the component or by adding anti-tampering features.

contents.html: 8.9 Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring (SACM)
contents.html_ja: 8.9 セキュリティの自動化と継続的監視（SACM）
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p63と照合。見出し

contents.html: There are several approved and draft SACM standards. Most are specifically relevant to IoT systems. Approved standards include: IEC TR 62443-2-3:2015 for requirements for asset owners and industrial automation and control system (IACS) product suppliers that have established and are now maintaining an IACS patch management program; and the IETF RFC 7632 with use cases for securely aggregating configuration and operational data and evaluating that data to determine an organization's security posture. IETF Active Internet Drafts include: the Resource-Oriented Lightweight Information Exchange (ROLIE) Definition of the ROLIE Software Descriptor Extension; Concise Software Identifiers; Endpoint Compliance Profile; Software Inventory Message and Attributes (SWIMA) for PA-TNC; and Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring (SACM) Terminology.
contents.html_ja: 承認済みおよびドラフトの SACM 標準がいくつかあります。その大半は IoT システムに特に関連します。承認済み標準には、IACS のパッチ管理プログラムを確立し、現在維持している資産所有者と産業用オートメーションおよび制御システム（IACS）製品供給者に関する要件を扱う IEC TR 62443-2-3:2015 と、構成データと運用データを安全に集約し、そのデータを評価して組織のセキュリティ態勢を判断するためのユースケースを示す IETF RFC 7632 があります。IETF の有効なインターネットドラフトには、Resource-Oriented Lightweight Information Exchange（ROLIE）Definition of the ROLIE Software Descriptor Extension、Concise Software Identifiers、Endpoint Compliance Profile、Software Inventory Message and Attributes（SWIMA）for PA-TNC、Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring（SACM）Terminology があります。

contents.html_ja: IoT 機器の資源の制限（メモリ、プロセッサー、電力）により、継続的監視に対するエージェントベースの手法の実装が困難になる場合があります。より高度な機能が開発されるにつれて、機器製造者は価格と性能を考慮する必要が生じます。IoT エコシステムは異種混在であり、標準が整備され広く採用されるまでは、機器製造者とセキュリティベンダーは、監視のための機器固有のエージェントとインターフェースの開発に投資する必要があります。
contents.html: The resource limitations of IoT devices (memory, processor, power) can make it difficult to implement agent-based approaches to continuous monitoring. Device manufacturers will need to consider price and performance as more advanced capabilities are developed. The IoT ecosystem is heterogeneous and until standards are in place and broadly adopted, device manufacturers and security vendors will need to make investments in developing device-specific agents and interfaces for monitoring.

contents.html: There are many approved or draft system security engineering standards. Some are relevant to IoT systems or specific IoT systems (e.g., healthcare). Examples include: ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2015 for a set of systems engineering processes and associated terminology; the ISA/IEC 62443 series for Industrial Automation and Control Systems (IACS) that includes security management requirements.
contents.html_ja: 承認済みまたはドラフトのシステムセキュリティエンジニアリング標準は数多くあります。一部は IoT システムまたは特定の IoT システム（例: ヘルスケア）に関連します。例には、システムエンジニアリングのプロセス群と関連用語のための ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288:2015、セキュリティマネジメント要件を含む産業用オートメーションおよび制御システム（IACS）のための ISA/IEC 62443 シリーズがあります。

contents.html: The functional description of IoT (Section 4) in this report provides a starting point for assessing and improving the current state of international cybersecurity standards development for IoT. It may also serve as a basis for future understanding and communications among agencies about IoT and cybersecurity-related challenges and solutions.

contents.html: Several IoT applications have been reviewed in this report to better understand IoT cybersecurity objectives, risks, and threats. From this review, it appears that many IoT systems, which have been developed for diverse agency missions, share common cybersecurity threats. Specific IoT applications may face additional classes of threats. Cybersecurity risk assessments need to be based upon an IoT application’s priorities for confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information.
contents.html_ja: IoT のサイバーセキュリティ目的、リスク、および脅威をよりよく理解するため、本報告書ではいくつかの IoT アプリケーションを検討しました。この検討から、多様な機関の任務のために開発された多くの IoT システムには、共通するサイバーセキュリティ上の脅威があると考えられます。特定の IoT アプリケーションは、追加の種類の脅威に直面する場合があります。サイバーセキュリティリスクアセスメントは、情報の機密性、完全性、可用性に関する IoT アプリケーションの優先事項に基づく必要があります。

contents.html: With the continuing, rapid innovation of IT, the inventory of IoT-relevant cybersecurity standards will remain dynamic. Annex D of this report lists international cybersecurity standards that the IoT Task Group has identified to be IoT relevant. The listing is substantial but it is not being represented as complete. It is also a one-time, static listing. The standards have been organized by the 12 core areas of cybersecurity described in this report (Section 7). The substantial number of standards for some of the core cybersecurity areas are the result of IT innovation as well as competitive solutions for various technologies. Based upon the information in Annex D, a high-level summary has been developed of IoT-relevant cybersecurity standards including market impact, where known, and possible standards gaps (Section 8).
contents.html_ja: IT の急速なイノベーションが続くなか、IoT に関連するサイバーセキュリティ標準の一覧は、今後も動的であり続けます。本報告書の Annex D は、IoT タスクグループが IoT に関連すると特定した国際サイバーセキュリティ標準を一覧にしています。この一覧は相当な量ですが、網羅的なものとして示されているわけではありません。また、これは一時点の静的な一覧です。標準は、本報告書で説明した 12 のサイバーセキュリティのコア領域（セクション 7）ごとに整理されています。一部のサイバーセキュリティのコア領域で標準が相当な数にのぼるのは、IT のイノベーションの結果であるとともに、さまざまな技術に対する競合するソリューションの結果でもあります。Annex D の情報に基づき、IoT に関連するサイバーセキュリティ標準について、わかっている範囲での市場への影響と、標準に存在しうるギャップを含む、高レベルの要約をまとめました（セクション 8）。

contents.html: Also, in accordance with federal policy, agencies should support the development of appropriate conformity assessment schemes to the requirements in such standards. U.S. industry has a rich history of developing conformity assessment (CA) programs to meet our society’s needs. In the IT sector for example, the Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> logo appearing on wireless network devices shows that the product has been tested and certified by the Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> Alliance, a non-profit member association, whose goal is to ensure that any device carrying the logo connect seamlessly to any Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> network. Many consumers may not understand the technical details of Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup>, but they have confidence that the logo ensures that the device will connect to their home networks.
contents.html_ja: また、連邦政策に従い、各機関は、これらの標準の要件に対する適切な適合性評価スキームの策定を支援すべきです。米国の産業界には、社会のニーズを満たす適合性評価（CA）プログラムを策定してきた豊かな歴史があります。たとえば IT 分野では、無線ネットワーク機器に表示される Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> ロゴは、その製品が、非営利の会員団体である Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> Alliance によってテストされ認証されたことを示します。同団体の目標は、ロゴを付けたあらゆる機器が、あらゆる Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> ネットワークにシームレスに接続できることを確保することです。多くの消費者は Wi-Fi<sup>TM</sup> の技術的な詳細を理解していないかもしれませんが、ロゴによってその機器が自宅のネットワークに接続できることが保証されるという確信を持っています。

contents.html: The decision on the type, independence and technical rigor of conformity assessment for IoT should be risk-based. The need for confidence in conformity must be balanced with the cost to the public and private sectors, including their international operations and legal obligations. Successful conformity assessment provides the needed level of confidence, is efficient, and has a sustainable and scalable business model.

contents.html_ja: システムは、運輸から公共事業、通信に至るまで、米国社会のあらゆる側面を支えており、世界中からアクセスでき、多くの場合は制御もできます。より多くの機器がネットワークに接続され、それらのネットワークが相互に接続されており、この概念は IoT として知られています。しかし、この傾向を表すこの名称の使用について合意がないのと同様に、IoT の普遍的な定義もありません。IoT、インダストリアルインターネット、サイバーフィジカルシステム（CPS）のいずれと呼ばれるにせよ、この用語は、さまざまな情報を感知し、記録し、解釈し、通信し、処理し、それに基づいて行動したり、物理環境の機器を制御したりできる、オブジェクト（または機器）、アプリケーション、サービスの分散型ネットワークを表します。これらの機器は、消費者向け機器の小型センサーから、産業用制御システム（ICS）の高度なコンピューターまで、多岐にわたります。最終的に、これらの機器は、直接的であれ、接続された機械装置を通じてであれ、物理世界に何らかの運動的な影響を及ぼします。
contents.html: Systems underpin every facet of American society—from transportation to utilities to communications—and are accessible and often controllable from around the world. More devices are connected to networks, and those networks are connected to each other, a concept known as IoT; however, there is no universal definition of IoT, just as there is no agreement in the use of that name to describe this trend. Whether it is called IoT, the Industrial Internet, or cyber-physical systems (CPS), the term describes a decentralized network of objects (or devices), applications, and services that can sense, log, interpret, communicate, process, and act on a variety of information or control devices in the physical environment. These devices range from small sensors on consumer devices to sophisticated computers in industrial control systems (ICS). Ultimately, the devices have some type of kinetic impact on the physical world, whether directly or through a mechanical device to which they are connected.

contents.html: It is important to understand what the Internet of Things is and what the difference is between IoT ecosystem and an IoT system. contents.html_ja: このグリーンペーパーでは、引き続き、モノのインターネットという用語を、膨大な数の機器が相互に、またはインターネットに接続されるという技術的発展を指す包括的な用語として使用します。これは、この用語が広く使われ、一般に受け入れられていることを踏まえたものです。一部のコメント提出者が指摘したように、この用語自体は誤った呼称です。モノのインターネットに含まれる機器の多くは、インターネットプロトコルを使用していないか、あるいはいずれにせよ、インターネットに直接接続しない場合があるためです。IoT という用語は、実際のモノよりも、システムやネットワークを記述していることがあります。IoT は、ここで論じる技術と関連する問題について一般に使われる用語となっており、簡潔にするため、この文書全体で使用します。
contents.html: This green paper will continue to use the term Internet of Things as an umbrella term to reference the technological development in which a greatly increasing number of devices are connected to one another and/or to the Internet. This acknowledges the widespread use and general popular acceptance of the term. The term itself is, as pointed out by some commenters, a misnomer, as many of the devices included in the Internet of Things do not use Internet Protocol or in any event may not connect directly to the Internet. At times, IoT term is more descriptive of the system or network than an actual thing. IoT has become the commonly used term for the technologies and related issues discussed here, and for the sake of simplicity it will be used throughout this paper.

contents.html_ja: IoT の運用、信頼性、ライフサイクルを規律する構成要素について、形式的、分析的な、あるいは記述的な一式さえ存在しません。「IoT の根底にある科学とは、仮にあるとして何か」という問いに答えるには、すべてではないにせよ大半の「モノ」のネットワークに共通する原則を定義する、構成可能性のモデルと語彙が必要です。この文書は、IoT がセンシング、計算、通信、アクチュエーションを伴うという考えに基づき、IoT の根底にある基礎的な科学を提示します。
contents.html: There is no formal, analytic, or even descriptive set of the building blocks that govern the operation, trustworthiness, and lifecycle of IoT. A composability model and vocabulary that defines principles common to most, if not all networks of things, is needed to address the question: “what is the science, if any, underlying IoT?” This document offers an underlying and foundational science to IoT based on a belief that IoT involves sensing, computing, communication, and actuation.

contents.html: Some SDOs require two or more implementations before final approval of a standard. Such implementations may or may not be commercial products or services. In other cases, an SDO may be developing a standard while conforming commercial products or services are already being sold. Innovation in IT means that IT standards are constantly being developed, approved, and maintained. Revisions to previous editions of standards may or may not be backward-compatible. An SDO approved standard does not necessarily equate with success. Widespread market acceptance of an approved standard is the goal.

Cryptographic Techniques: Techniques and mechanisms and their associated standards are used to provide: confidentiality; entity authentication; non-repudiation; key management; data integrity; trust worthy data platforms; message authentication; and digital signatures.
DocumentsSDODescriptionMaturity Level (Table 6)
QSC is a rapidly growing area of research. There are already academic conference series such as PQC and workshops have been established by ETSI/IQC [i.1] and NIST. The European Commission has recently granted funding to two QSC projects under the Horizon 2020 framework: SAFEcrypto [i.2] and PQCrypto [i.3] and [i.4]. The present document draws on all these research efforts.
The present document will cover three main areas. Clauses 4 and 5 discuss the types of primitives being considered and describe an assessment framework; clauses 6 to 10 discuss some representative cryptographic primitives; and clause 11 gives a preliminary discussion of key sizes.
ETSI GR QSC 003 V1.1.1 (2017-02)ETSIQuantum Safe Cryptography; Case Studies and Deployment Scenarios
The present document examines a number of real-world uses cases for the deployment of quantum-safe cryptography (QSC). Specifically, it examines some typical applications where cryptographic primitives are deployed today and discusses some points for consideration by developers, highlighting features that may need change to accommodate quantum-safe cryptography. The main focus of the document is on options for upgrading public-key primitives for key establishment and authentication, although several alternative, non-public-key options are also discussed.
The present document gives an overview of different technology areas; identify where the security and cryptography currently resides; and indicate how things may have to evolve to support quantum-safe cryptographic primitives. Clauses five and six discuss network security protocols, using TLS and S/MIME as typical examples. These are contrasted in clauses seven and eight by an examination of security options for IoT and Satellite use cases, which have very different requirements and constraints than traditional Internet-type services. Some alternatives to public key protocols are reviewed in clause nine. Authentication requirements are discussed in		Approved Standard

DocumentsSDODescriptionMaturity Level (Table 6)
  1. Initiation: to initiate authentication the authenticator will periodically transmit EAP-Request Identity frames to a special Layer 2 address on the local network segment.
  2. Negotiation: The authentication server sends a reply to the authenticator, containing an EAP Request specifying the EAP Method. The authenticator encapsulates the EAP Request in an Extensible Authentication Protocol over LAN (EAPOL) frame and transmits it to the supplicant. At this point the supplicant can start using the requested EAP Method, or do an NAK ("Negative Acknowledgement") and respond with the EAP Methods it is willing to perform.
  3. Authentication: If the authentication server and supplicant agree on an EAP Method, EAP Requests and Responses are sent between the supplicant and the authentication server (translated by the authenticator) until the authentication server responds with either an EAP-Success message (encapsulated in a RADIUS Access-Accept packet), or an EAP-Failure message (encapsulated in a RADIUS Access-Reject packet). If authentication is successful, the authenticator sets the port to the "authorized" state and normal traffic is allowed, if it is unsuccessful the port remains in the "unauthorized" state. When the supplicant logs off, it sends an EAPOL-logoff message to the authenticator, the authenticator then sets the port to the "unauthorized" state, once again blocking all non-EAP traffic.

  1. Balanced password-authenticated key agreement – two parties share a common password and they want to prove to each other that they know the password, and only then engage in secure communications, without revealing the password to others.
  2. Augmented password-authenticated key agreement methods – similar to the first except that one of the parties, the Server, has password verification data derived using a one-way function of the password.
  3. Password- authenticated key retrieval – addresses the scenario where one desires to further decrease the sensitivity of stored password-derived data.
All these methods require one or more parties to use specific password-related data to make the method succeed.
Primitives: The following types of primitives are defined in this standard:

  • Secret value derivation primitives (SVDP), components of augmented password-authenticated key agreement and PKRSs
  • Password verification data generation primitives (PVDGP), components of augmented password-authenticated key agreement schemes (APKAS)
  • Key retrieval blinding primitives (KRBP), key retrieval unblinding primitives (KRUP), and key retrieval permutation primitives (KRPP), components of key retrieval schemes.

  • シークレット値導出プリミティブ（SVDP）。拡張型パスワード認証付き鍵合意と PKRS の構成要素

Security Considerations:
The secure transmission of circuit more services in DECT (Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications) is based on the DSAA2 (DECT Standard Authentication Algorithm #2) and DSC/DSC2 (DECT Standard Cipher/DECT Standard Cipher #2) specifications developed by ETSI Technical Committee (TC) DECT and the ETSI Security Algorithms Group of Experts (SAGE).
DECT ULE communications are secured at the link layer (DLC) by encryption and per-message authentication through CCM (Counter with Cipher Block Chaining Message Authentication Code (CBC-MAC)) mode. The underlying algorithm for providing encryption and authentication is AES128.
The DECT ULE (Digital Enhances Cordless Telecommunications Ultra Low Energy) pairing procedure generates a master User Authentication Key (UAK). During the location registration procedure, or when the permanent virtual circuits are established, the session security keys are generated. Both the master authentication key and session security keys are generated by use of the DSAA2 algorithm, which uses AES127 as the underlying algorithm.

  • 真のアイデンティティを認証、検証、証明するシステムを構築すること。
  • 受動的で防御的なネットワークセキュリティから、能動的に管理されるサイバーセキュリティへと転換すること。

  • ソフトウェアの真正性と、ソフトウェアのアイデンティティとソフトウェアデータの一貫性を証明し、トラステッドコンピューティングを実現すること。
  • 信頼できる接続は、信頼できるシステムの鍵です。信頼できるルーティングは、信頼できる接続を実現する鍵です。

September 2016 or later		TCGTrusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0
What is TPM 2.0?
An International standard (also published as ISO/IEC 11889:2015) that enables trust in computing platforms in general by receiving commands
The TPM 2.0 provides support for a wide array of cryptographic operations including hashing, symmetric and asymmetric encryption, key generation, digital signatures, random number generation, protected storage and protected capabilities. The TPM architecture is cryptographic agile with support for numerous algorithms and curves with an extensible model to add more algorithms or curves as needed. The TPM 2.0 standard uses a library model so simpler profiles for a particular purpose can be defined using a subset of the available algorithms and capabilities to address platform specific requirements or constraints like Mobile, Automotive or IoT.
The TPM 2.0 can create Endorsement Keys that serve as a statically unique TPM identity or an identity for an IoT component that a TPM is bound to. TPM manufacturers may also issue Endorsement Key certificates to provide confidence to third parties that interaction with a TPM is based on an implementation provided by the manufacturer issuing the certificate. TPM generated keys can be used for device authentication and cryptographically associated with Endorsement Keys in a TPM.
TPM 2.0 supports anonymous remote attestation to help remote entities validate IoT component software measurements stored in a TPM during the boot process or based on the dynamic launch of a measured component. Remote attestation and its local equivalent called sealing provide evidence of IoT component integrity for both code and configuration.		Approved Standard

コマンドを受け取ることで、コンピューティングプラットフォーム全般への信頼を可能にする国際標準（ISO/IEC 11889:2015 としても発行されています）。
TPM 2.0 は、ハッシュ化、共通鍵暗号と非対称鍵暗号、鍵生成、デジタル署名、乱数生成、保護されたストレージ、保護された機能など、幅広い暗号操作に対応しています。TPM のアーキテクチャは、多数のアルゴリズムと曲線に対応する暗号アジリティを備えており、必要に応じてアルゴリズムや曲線を追加できる拡張可能なモデルを持っています。TPM 2.0 標準はライブラリモデルを使用しているため、モバイル、自動車、IoT など、プラットフォーム固有の要件や制約に対処するために、利用可能なアルゴリズムと機能の部分集合を用いて、特定の目的のためのより単純なプロファイルを定義できます。
TPM 2.0 は、静的に一意の TPM アイデンティティ、または TPM が結び付けられた IoT コンポーネントのアイデンティティとして機能する Endorsement Key を作成できます。TPM 製造者は、TPM とのやり取りが、証明書を発行する製造者が提供する実装に基づくものであるという確信を第三者に与えるため、Endorsement Key の証明書を発行する場合もあります。TPM が生成した鍵は、機器の認証に使用でき、TPM 内で Endorsement Key と暗号的に関連付けられます。
TPM 2.0 は、リモートのエンティティが、ブート処理中に TPM に保存された、または計測済みコンポーネントの動的な起動に基づく IoT コンポーネントのソフトウェア計測値を検証するのを助ける、匿名のリモートアテステーションに対応しています。リモートアテステーションと、そのローカル版であるシーリングは、コードと構成の両方について、IoT コンポーネントの完全性の証拠を提供します。		Approved Standard

MUDIETFManufacturer Usage Description (MUD) Specification
The MUD Specification is a scalable network security application specification.
The goal of MUD is to provide a means for end devices to signal to the network what sort of access and network functionality they require to properly function. The initial focus is on access control.
The MUD supporting network controller enforces security policies derived from a policy file originally provided by the IoT device manufacturer. Moreover, the MUD controller can enforce security policies for classes of devices. For example, the MUD controller can ensure that an IP camera communicates with its monitoring station server only. If physical compromise of the IP camera attempts to divert video streaming to an adversary server, the MUD controller will block and flag these attempts, assuming correct implementation of the MUD file and network administration.		Under Development

Identity and Identity Protection:
Public-key ciphers can be used to establishing a longer-term cyber identity, e.g., for authentication. In public-key cryptography, keys come in matched pairs (public key and private key) for each user, entity, computer, or subject. The private key must be accessible only to the subject and represents the subject’s digital identity in cyberspace.
Hashes can be used to verify the integrity of code modules by taking the hash of the good known code module and using that to identify the module (like a unique global name).
The private key of someone’s key pair is like their digital identity. Private keys must be kept confidential in order to protect someone’s digital identity.

What is TPM 2.0?
An International standard (also published as ISO/IEC 11889:2015) that enables trust in computing platforms in general by receiving commands
The TPM 2.0 provides support for a wide array of cryptographic operations including hashing, symmetric and asymmetric encryption, key generation, digital signatures, random number generation, protected storage and protected capabilities. The TPM architecture is cryptographic agile with support for numerous algorithms and curves with an extensible model to add more algorithms or curves as needed. The TPM 2.0 standard uses a library model so simpler profiles for a particular purpose can be defined using a subset of the available algorithms and capabilities to address platform specific requirements or constraints like Mobile, Automotive or IoT.
The TPM 2.0 can create Endorsement Keys that serve as a statically unique TPM identity or an identity for an IoT component that a TPM is bound to. TPM manufacturers may also issue Endorsement Key certificates to provide confidence to third parties that interaction with a TPM is based on an implementation provided by the manufacturer issuing the certificate. TPM generated keys can be used for device authentication and cryptographically associated with Endorsement Keys in a TPM.O

TPM 2.0 とは何か。
コマンドを受け取ることで、コンピューティングプラットフォーム全般への信頼を可能にする国際標準（ISO/IEC 11889:2015 としても発行されています）。
TPM 2.0 は、ハッシュ化、共通鍵暗号と公開鍵暗号、鍵生成、デジタル署名、乱数生成、保護されたストレージ、保護された機能など、幅広い暗号操作に対応しています。TPM のアーキテクチャは、多数のアルゴリズムと曲線に対応する暗号アジリティを備えており、必要に応じてアルゴリズムや曲線を追加できる拡張可能なモデルを持っています。TPM 2.0 標準はライブラリモデルを使用しているため、モバイル、自動車、IoT など、プラットフォーム固有の要件や制約に対処するために、利用可能なアルゴリズムと機能の部分集合を用いて、特定の目的のためのより単純なプロファイルを定義できます。

DocumentsSDODescriptionMaturity Level (Table 6)
User Attribute Definition: this family defines the requirements for associating user security attributes with users as needed to support the TSF in making security decisions. Specification of Secrets: this family defines requirements for mechanisms that enforce defined quality metrics on provided secrets and generate secrets to satisfy the defined metric.
User Authentication: this family defines the types of user authentication mechanisms supported by the TSF.
User Identification: defines the conditions under which users shall be required to identify themselves before performing any other actions that are to be mediated by the TSF and which require user identification.
Page 87, Section 12
Class FCS: Cryptographic Support:
The TSF (TOE Security Functionality) may employ cryptographic functionality to help satisfy several high-level security objectives. These include (but are not limited to): identification and authentication, non-repudiation, trusted path, trusted channel, and data separation.
This class is composed of two families: FCS_CKM and FCS_COP.
Cryptographic Key Management (FCS_CKM): intended to support the lifecycle of cryptographic keys and defines requirements for: cryptographic key generation, cryptographic key distribution, cryptographic key access and cryptographic key destruction.

文書SDO説明成熟度レベル（表 6）
ユーザー属性定義: このファミリーは、TSF がセキュリティ上の決定を行うのを支えるために必要な、ユーザーのセキュリティ属性とユーザーを関連付けるための要件を定義します。シークレットの仕様: このファミリーは、提供されたシークレットに対して定義された品質メトリクスを強制し、定義されたメトリクスを満たすシークレットを生成するメカニズムの要件を定義します。
ユーザー認証: このファミリーは、TSF が対応するユーザー認証メカニズムの種類を定義します。
ユーザー識別: TSF が仲介し、ユーザー識別を必要とする他のあらゆる動作を実行する前に、ユーザーが自らを識別することを求められる条件を定義します。
87 ページ、セクション 12
Class FCS: 暗号サポート:
TSF（TOE セキュリティ機能）は、いくつかの高水準のセキュリティ目的を満たすのに役立てるため、暗号機能を使用する場合があります。これらには、識別と認証、否認防止、トラステッドパス、トラステッドチャネル、データ分離が含まれます（ただしこれらに限定されません）。

DTSec helps to assess the impact of threats and vulnerabilities on device functionality and end users/patients by requiring developers to consider relevant threats and how they might impact safe clinical use.
DTSec also helps assess the impact of vulnerabilities discovered during the security evaluation program
DTSec also helps stakeholders balance the need for security with essential clinical performance.

DTSec helps to assess the likelihood of a vulnerability being exploited. As part of the vulnerability assessment requirement included in the Protection Profiles and Security Targets, the security evaluator will attempt to understand not only whether a vulnerability is exploitable but also what level of attack potential is required to exploit.

資産、脅威、脆弱性の特定:
DTSec は ISO 15408 を活用して、開発者が、ISO 15408 の標準化された枠組みを用いて、医療機器の製品とコンポーネントに適用される脅威を特定し、文書化するのを支援します。
DTSec の評価による保証プログラムは、開発者のセキュアな開発ライフサイクルに、資格のあるサイバーセキュリティのテストラボによる独立した脆弱性評価を加えることで、開発者が脆弱性を特定するのを支援します。
脅威と脆弱性が機器の機能とエンドユーザー／患者に及ぼす影響の評価:
DTSec は、開発者に、関連する脅威と、それらが安全な臨床使用にどのような影響を及ぼしうるかを考慮することを求めることで、脅威と脆弱性が機器の機能とエンドユーザー／患者に及ぼす影響の評価を支援します。
DTSec は、セキュリティ評価プログラム中に発見された脆弱性の影響の評価も支援します。
DTSec は、利害関係者が、セキュリティの必要性と不可欠な臨床性能との均衡を取るのも支援します。
脅威や脆弱性が悪用される可能性の評価:
DTSec は、脆弱性が悪用される可能性の評価を支援します。プロテクションプロファイルとセキュリティターゲットに含まれる脆弱性評価要件の一環として、セキュリティ評価者は、脆弱性が悪用可能かどうかだけでなく、悪用するためにどのレベルの攻撃能力が必要かについても理解しようとします。

In a 6LoWPAN stack, sensitive information will normally be protected by transport- or application-layer (or even IP-layer) security, which are all above the adaptation layer, leaving no sensitive information to compress at the GHC level. However, a 6LoWPAN deployment that entirely depends on Media Access Control (MAC) layer security may be vulnerable to attacks that exploit redundancy information disclosed by compression to recover information about secret values. This attack is fully mitigated by not exposing secret values to the adaptation layer or by not using GHC in deployments where this is done.

DocumentsSDODescriptionMaturity Level (Table 6)
Risk Management:
When designing the product, the vendor shall establish and document a security risk analysis for the product, containing:
  • An identification of all product functionalities and all data stored, processed or used by the product
  • A list of all threats for the product, its functionalities and data
  • An assessment of the impact of each identified threat, should it become a reality
  • An assessment of the likelihood of each identified threat
  • A determination of the resulting risk level of each threat, considering its impact and likelihood
  • Risk acceptance criteria, i.e., clear criteria to determine whether or not a given risk level is acceptable.
  • A determination of suitable risk controls to mitigate each threat with an unacceptable risk level
  • An assessment of the residual risk level for each threat after application of these risk controls.
  • The vendor shall document a risk evaluation method for the possible presence of known (types of) vulnerabilities in the product
  • If the vendor has allowed for the presence of any known vulnerabilities in the product, the vendor’s security risk analysis for the product shall contain a description of each accepted known vulnerability.

リスクマネジメント:
製品を設計する際、ベンダーは、次のものを含む、製品のセキュリティリスク分析を確立し、文書化しなければなりません。
  • 製品のすべての機能と、製品が保存、処理、または使用するすべてのデータの特定
  • 製品、その機能、およびデータに対するすべての脅威の一覧
  • 特定された各脅威が現実のものとなった場合の影響の評価
  • 特定された各脅威の可能性の評価
  • 影響と可能性を考慮した、各脅威の結果としてのリスクレベルの決定
  • リスク受容基準、すなわち、特定のリスクレベルが受容可能かどうかを判断する明確な基準。
  • 受容できないリスクレベルの各脅威を緩和するための、適切なリスク管理策の決定
  • これらのリスク管理策の適用後の、各脅威の残留リスクレベルの評価。
  • ベンダーは、製品に既知の（種類の）脆弱性が存在する可能性についての、リスク評価方法を文書化しなければなりません。
  • ベンダーが、製品に既知の脆弱性が存在することを許容した場合、ベンダーの製品のセキュリティリスク分析には、受容された各既知の脆弱性の説明を含めなければなりません。

Security Services: the security association protocols shall be based on the Diffie-Hellman key exchange employing the elliptic curve public key cryptography.
  • Master key pre-shared association – a node and a hub shall each have a secret pre-shared MK prior to running the MK pre-shared association protocol to activate their pre-shared MK as their shared MK for their creation.
  • Unauthenticated association – a node and a hub shall each require no authentication credentials such as a shared secret or human intervention prior to running the unauthenticated association protocol to generate their shared MK for their Pairwise Transient Key (PTK) creation.
  • Public key hidden association – a node and a hub shall have a secured, secret transfer of the node’s public key to the hub, typically through an out-of-band channel, prior to running the public key hidden association protocol to generate their shared MK for their PTK creation.
  • Password authenticated association – a node and a hub shall each have a secret shared password prior to running the password authenticated association protocol to generate their shared MK for their PTK creation.
  • Display authenticated association – a node and a hub shall each have a display of a 5-digit decimal number prior to running the display authenticated association protocol to generate their shared MK for their PTK creation.

Risk of Amplification: An attacker might use CoAP nodes to turn a small attack packet into a larger attack packet, an approach known as amplification. There is therefore a danger that CoAP nodes could become implicated in denial-of-service attacks by using the amplifying properties of the protocol. As a mitigating factor, many constrained networks will only be able to generate a small amount of traffic, which may make CoAP nodes less attractive for this attack. Therefore, large amplification factors should not be provided in the response if the request is not authenticated.
IP Address Spoofing Attacks: Due to the lack of handshake in UDP, a rogue endpoint that is free to read and write messages carried by the constrained network may easily attack a single endpoint, a group of endpoints, as well as a whole network. Response spoofing by off-path attackers can be detected and mitigated even without transport later security by choosing a nontrivial, randomized token in the request.

増幅のリスク: 攻撃者は、CoAP ノードを使って小さな攻撃パケットを大きな攻撃パケットに変えることができ、この手法は増幅として知られています。したがって、CoAP ノードがプロトコルの増幅特性を利用して、サービス拒否攻撃に関与させられる危険があります。緩和要因として、多くの制約のあるネットワークは少量のトラフィックしか生成できないため、CoAP ノードはこの攻撃の標的として魅力が低いかもしれません。そのため、要求が認証されていない場合は、応答に大きな増幅率を持たせるべきではありません。
IP アドレススプーフィング攻撃: UDP にはハンドシェイクがないため、制約のあるネットワークが運ぶメッセージを自由に読み書きできる不正なエンドポイントは、単一のエンドポイント、エンドポイントのグループ、ネットワーク全体を、容易に攻撃できる可能性があります。パス外の攻撃者によるレスポンスのスプーフィングは、要求内で自明でないランダム化されたトークンを選択することで、トランスポート層のセキュリティがなくても、検知し緩和できます。

Network Security: Standards that provide security requirements and guidelines on processes and methods for the secure management, operation and use of information, information networks, and their inter-connections.
DocumentsSDODescriptionMaturity Level (Table 6)
When TLS is used: SSL Certificates sent from the Client can be used by the Server to authenticate the Client.
When VPN is used: between the Clients and Servers, VPN can provide confidence that data is only being received from authorized Clients.
Authentication of the Server by the Client: The MQTT protocol is not trust symmetrical; it provides no mechanism for the Client to authenticate the Server,
When TLS is used: SSL Certificates sent from the Server can be used by the Client to authenticate the Server.
When VPN is used: between Clients and Servers, VPN can provide confidence that Clients are connecting to the intended Server.
Page 61, Sections 5.4.1 & 5.4.3
Note: MQTT does not provide any of these services. The standard recommends that other standards be applied, e.g., TLS.
Integrity of Application Messages and Control Packets:
Application Messages: applications can independently include hash values in the messages. This can provide integrity of the contents of Publish Control Packets across the network and at rest.
When TLS is used: provides hash algorithms to verify the integrity of data sent over the network.

TLS を使用する場合: クライアントから送信された SSL 証明書を、サーバーがクライアントの認証に使用できます。
VPN を使用する場合: クライアントとサーバーの間で、VPN により、データが認可されたクライアントからのみ受信されているという確信を得られます。
クライアントによるサーバーの認証: MQTT プロトコルは信頼が対称的ではなく、クライアントがサーバーを認証するメカニズムを提供しません。
TLS を使用する場合: サーバーから送信された SSL 証明書を、クライアントがサーバーの認証に使用できます。
VPN を使用する場合: クライアントとサーバーの間で、VPN により、クライアントが意図したサーバーに接続しているという確信を得られます。
61 ページ、セクション 5.4.1 & 5.4.3
注: MQTT は、これらのサービスをいずれも提供しません。この標準は、TLS など他の標準を適用することを推奨しています。
アプリケーションメッセージと制御パケットの完全性:
アプリケーションメッセージ: アプリケーションは、メッセージにハッシュ値を独自に含めることができます。これにより、Publish 制御パケットの内容の完全性を、ネットワーク上でも保存中でも確保できます。

ZigBee IP offers extensive security features, including PANA/EAP based network authentication and admission control, network re-keying, AES-128-CCM based layer 2 encryption, and TLS application layer authentication and encryption.
ZigBee IP is the first open standards-based IPv6 specification for wireless sensor networks. The ZigBee alliance made a significant investment to bring IPv6 network protocols to IEEE 802.15.4 wireless mesh networks.
The ZigBee IP specification offers a scalable architecture with end-to-end IPv6 networking based on standard Internet protocols, such as 6LowPAN, IPv6, PANA, RPL, TCP, TLS and UDP to a create cost-effective and energy-efficient wireless mesh network.

DocumentsSDODescriptionMaturity Level (Table 6)
SUITIETFSoftware Updates for Internet of Things (SUIT)
Vulnerabilities in Internet of Things (IoT) devices have raised the need
for a secure firmware update mechanism that is also suitable for constrained
devices. Security experts, researchers, and regulators recommend that all IoT
devices be equipped with such a mechanism. While there are many proprietary
firmware update mechanisms in use today, there is no modern interoperable
approach allowing secure updates to firmware in IoT devices.
This group will focus on defining a firmware update solution (taking into account past learnings from RFC 4108 and other firmware update solutions) that will be usable on Class 1 (as defined in RFC 7228) devices, i.e., devices with ~10 KiB RAM and ~100 KiB flash. The solution may apply to more capable devices as well.		Under Development
TEEPIETFTrusted Execution Environment Provisioning (TEEP)
The Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) is a secure area of a processor. The TEE provides security features such as isolated execution and integrity of Trusted Applications, along with provisions for maintaining the confidentiality of their assets. In general terms, the TEE offers an execution space that provides a higher level of security than a "rich" operating system and more functionality than a secure element.		Under Development

This standard can be freely downloaded.		Approved Standard

SUITIETFSoftware Updates for Internet of Things (SUIT)
モノのインターネット（IoT）機器の脆弱性により、制約のある機器にも適した、安全なファームウェア更新メカニズムの
必要性が生じています。セキュリティの専門家、研究者、規制当局は、すべての IoT 機器にそのようなメカニズムを
備えることを推奨しています。現在、独自の
ファームウェア更新メカニズムが数多く使用されていますが、IoT 機器のファームウェアを
安全に更新できる、最新の相互運用可能な

TEEPIETFTrusted Execution Environment Provisioning (TEEP)
Trusted Execution Environment（TEE）は、プロセッサー内の安全な領域です。TEE は、信頼されたアプリケーションの隔離された実行や完全性などのセキュリティ機能を、それらの資産の機密性を維持するための備えとともに提供します。一般的に言えば、TEE は、「リッチ」なオペレーティングシステムよりも高いレベルのセキュリティを提供し、セキュアエレメントよりも多くの機能を備えた実行空間を提供します。		Under Development

contents.html: The applicability sections of each FIPS publication should be reviewed to determine if the publication is mandatory for federal agency use. FIPS publications do not apply to national security systems (as defined in Title III, Information Security, of FISMA). Federal government statutes (e.g., FISMA 2014), regulations, and policies (e.g., Office of Management and Budget [OMB] Circular A-130) may specify whether federal agencies are required, or encouraged, to comply with NIST’s SP 800-series publications. NIST’s SP 800 series publications shall not apply to national security systems without the express approval of appropriate federal officials exercising policy authority over such systems.
contents.html_ja: 連邦機関による使用が必須かどうかを判断するため、各 FIPS 刊行物の適用範囲の節を確認すべきです。FIPS 刊行物は、国家安全保障システム（FISMA の Title III, Information Security で定義）には適用されません。連邦政府の法令（例: FISMA 2014）、規制、および方針（例: Office of Management and Budget［OMB］Circular A-130）は、連邦機関が NIST の SP 800 シリーズ刊行物に準拠することを求められるのか、推奨されるのかを規定する場合があります。NIST の SP 800 シリーズ刊行物は、そうしたシステムに対する方針上の権限を行使する適切な連邦政府職員の明示的な承認なしには、国家安全保障システムに適用してはなりません。

The Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) promotes the U.S. economy and public welfare by providing technical leadership for the Nation’s measurement and standards infrastructure. ITL develops tests, test methods, reference data, proof of concept implementations, and technical analyses to advance the development and productive use of information technology. ITL’s responsibilities include the development of management, administrative, technical, and physical standards and guidelines for the cost-effective security and privacy of other than national security-related information in federal information systems.
Abstract

The Interagency International Cybersecurity Standardization Working Group (IICS WG) was established in December 2015 by the National Security Council’s Cyber Interagency Policy Committee. Its purpose is to coordinate on major issues in international cybersecurity standardization and thereby enhance U.S. federal agency participation in the process.

Effective U.S. Government participation involves coordinating across the federal government and working with the U.S. private sector. The U.S. relies more heavily on the private sector for standards development than do many other countries. Companies and industry groups, academic institutions, professional societies, consumer groups, and other interested parties are major contributors to this process. Further, the many Standards Developing Organizations (SDOs) which provide the infrastructure for the standards development are overwhelmingly private sector organizations.

On April 25, 2017, the IICS WG established an Internet of Things (IoT) Task Group to determine the current state of international cybersecurity standards development for IoT. This report is intended for use by the working group member agencies to assist them in their standards planning and to help coordinate U.S. Government participation in international cybersecurity standardization for IoT. Other organizations may also find this document useful in their planning.

Executive Summary

The Interagency International Cyber Security Working Group (IICS WG) was created in response to recommendations contained in the 2015 Interagency Report on Strategic U.S. Government Engagement in International Standardization to Achieve U.S. Objectives for Cybersecurity (NIST Interagency Report 8074 Volume 1 [1]). This working group coordinates on major issues in international cybersecurity standardization. It established an Internet of Things (IoT) Task Group to develop this report on the status of international cybersecurity standards relevant to IoT.

The growth of network-connected devices, systems, and services comprising the IoT creates immense opportunities and benefits for our society [2]. However, to reap the great benefits of IoT and to minimize the potentially significant risks, these network-connected devices need to be secure and resilient. This depends in large part upon the timely availability and widespread adoption of clear and effective international cybersecurity standards.

Both the government and the broader public are intended audiences for this report, which aims to inform and enable policymakers, managers, and standards participants as they seek timely development and use of such standards in IoT components, systems, and related services. This report relies upon terms and definitions defined in Annex A – Terms and Definitions of NISTIR 8074 Volume 2 [3]. It aims to establish a common understanding of IoT components, systems and applications for which standards could be relevant. The report starts with a functional description of IoT components, which are the basic building blocks of IoT systems. To provide insights into the present state of IoT cybersecurity standardization, the report describes five IoT technology application areas. These areas are certainly not exhaustive, but they are sufficiently representative to use in analyzing the present state of IoT cybersecurity standardization:  Connected vehicle IoT enables vehicles, roads, and other infrastructure to communicate

and share vital transportation information.  Consumer IoT consists of IoT applications in residences as well as wearable and mobile devices.  Health IoT processes data derived from sources such as electronic health records and patient-generated health data.  Smart building IoT includes energy usage monitoring systems, physical access control security systems and lighting control systems.  Smart manufacturing IoT enables enterprise-wide integration of data, technology, advanced manufacturing capabilities, and cloud and other services. IoT cybersecurity objectives, risks, and threats are then analyzed for IoT applications in general and for each of the five illustrative IoT technology application areas. Cybersecurity objectives for traditional information technology (IT) systems generally prioritize Confidentiality, then Integrity, and lastly Availability. IoT systems cross multiple sectors as well as use cases within

those sectors. Accordingly, cybersecurity objectives may be prioritized very differently by various parties, depending on the application. The increased ubiquity of IoT components and systems heighten the risks they present. Standards-based cybersecurity risk management will continue to be a major factor in the trustworthiness of IoT applications. Analysis of the application areas makes it clear that cybersecurity for IoT is unique and requires tailoring existing standards and creating new standards to address challenges, for example: pop-up network connections, shared system components, the ability to change physical aspects of the environment, and related connections to safety. Building upon NISTIR 8074 Volume 2, this report describes 12 cybersecurity core areas and provides examples of relevant standards. The analysis is based on the information in Annex D, which maps cybersecurity standards that may be relevant for IoT systems to the dozen cybersecurity core areas. The annotated standards listings in Annex D are not exhaustive, but they represent an extensive effort to identify presently relevant IoT cybersecurity standards. The market impacts of existing standards are noted; possible gaps in standards are identified in Section 8. While the Annex D listing is a onetime snapshot, it should prove useful as a point of departure for maintaining awareness of the evolving standards landscape. A summary of the status of cybersecurity standardization for the five specific examples of IoT applications is provided in Table 4. The report’s conclusions focus upon the issue of standards gaps and the effective use of existing standards. For example, further standards work is needed to secure communications which leverage the Internet as the main gateway for IT to Operations Technology (OT). For identified priorities, agencies should work with industry to initiate new standards projects in Standards Developing Organizations (SDOs) to close such gaps. In accordance with U.S. Government policy [4], agencies should:
participate in the development of IoT cybersecurity standards,
cite appropriate standards in their procurements based upon their mission, and
work with industry to support the development of appropriate conformity assessment schemes to help assure that the requirements in such standards are met.

1 Introduction

The Internet of Things (IoT) has already changed the world for individuals, as consumers and citizens, as well as for governments and industry. The IoT is expected to provide more revolutionary capability and become more ubiquitous. Yet, the adoption of IoT brings cybersecurity risks that pose a significant threat to the Nation, to organizations, and to individuals1.

Securing IoT devices is a major challenge, as manufactures tend to focus on functionality, compatibility requirements, customer convenience, and time-to-market rather than security. Meanwhile, security threats are increasing. For example, Symantec reported a 600 % increase in attacks against IoT devices from 2016 to 2017 [5].

The President’s National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee (NSTAC) has examined the cybersecurity implications of IoT within the context of national security and emergency preparedness. This examination “found that IoT adoption will increase in both speed and scope, and that it will impact virtually all sectors of our society. Additionally, the NSTAC determined that there is a small—and rapidly closing—window to ensure that IoT is adopted in a way that maximizes security and minimizes risk. If the country fails to do so, it will be coping with the consequences for generations [6].”

The President’s Commission on Enhancing National Cybersecurity reached a similar conclusion: “The IoT facilitates linking an incredible range of devices and products to each other and the world. Although this connectivity has the potential to revolutionize most industries and many facets of everyday life, the possible harm that malicious actors could cause by exploiting these technologies to gain access to parts of our critical infrastructure, given the current state of cybersecurity, is immense [7].”

Our economy is increasingly global, complex, and interconnected. It is characterized by rapid advances in information technology (IT). IT products and services need to provide sufficient levels of cybersecurity and resilience. The timely availability of international cybersecurity standards is a dynamic and critical component for the cybersecurity and resilience of all information and communications systems and supporting infrastructures [1].

The growth of network-connected devices, systems, and services comprising the IoT creates immense opportunities and benefits for our society [2]. However, to reap the great benefits of IoT and to minimize the potentially significant risks, these network-connected devices need to be secure and resilient. This depends in large part upon the timely availability and widespread adoption of clear and effective international cybersecurity standards.

1 Cybersecurity is defined as “the prevention of damage to, unauthorized use of, exploitation of, and – if needed – the restoration of electronic information and communications systems, and the information they contain, in order to strengthen the confidentiality, integrity and availability of these systems” per NISTIR 8074 vol. 2
2 Scope

Consistent with U.S. Government policy, agencies are encouraged to support the development and use of voluntary consensus standards, which are developed by predominantly private sector led voluntary consensus standards bodies [4]. This report examines the current state of international cybersecurity standards development by voluntary consensus standards bodies for IoT. It distills IoT down to the simplest concepts and describes the nuances associated with these concepts. It acknowledges but does not focus on specific technologies or concerns associated with IoT such as societal impact, safety, or privacy.

This report recognizes that cybersecurity—and cybersecurity standards— can support individuals’ safety and privacy. For example, cybersecurity standards when applied to the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of personally identifiable information (PII) are an important component of protecting individuals’ privacy. However, privacy cannot be achieved solely by securing individuals’ PII (see Figure 1). As noted in NISTIR 8062, An Introduction to Privacy Engineering and Risk Management in Federal Systems, privacy concerns can arise from intentional or authorized processing of information about individuals, and in certain contexts, even measures used to secure PII can result in privacy issues [8].
